description: baseline 1 with the post-change file only, no diff

cases.note: The leading '^' anchor was removed from parseRegExp, so parse() now matches a trailing number+unit suffix anywhere in the string instead of requiring the entire string to match. E.g. parse('foo1kb') returns 1024 instead of null, and parse('1kb2gb') returns 2147483648 instead of the parseInt fallback value 1.

cases.note: The default-decimalPlaces guard was changed from `options.decimalPlaces !== undefined` to `options && true`, so passing any options object without `decimalPlaces` yields `toFixed(undefined)` (0 decimals) instead of the default 2. E.g. `bytes(1536, {})` returns '2KB' instead of '1.5KB' and `bytes(1024, {fixedDecimals: true})` returns '1KB' instead of '1.00KB'.

cases.note: parse() uses Math.floor(map[unit] * floatValue) where bytes@3.1.2 uses Math.round, so fractional parses such as bytes.parse('1.9kb') return 1945 instead of 1946. The existing suite only tests exactly-representable fractions, so it stays green.

In YAML_INTEGER_EXPLICIT_PATTERN$1 (the core !!int tag) the octal alternative lost its '?': [-+]0o[0-7]+ requires a sign, while the implicit pattern and the JSON variant ([-+]?0o[0-7]+) accept unsigned octal. As a result load('!!int 0o777') throws instead of returning 511.

cases.note: The only change from ms@2.1.3 is an added `case '':` in the minutes branch of parse(), which is unreachable: match[2] can never be an empty string, and even if it were, `(match[2] || 'ms')` would coerce it to 'ms' before the switch. The behaviour is identical to the released version.

The switch-to-lookup-table refactor in parse() is behaviorally identical: all 31 unit strings the regex can produce are present as own keys in multipliers with the correct multipliers, the hasOwnProperty guard makes the default case equivalent (undefined), and n*1 equals n for the ms case. All other functions match upstream ms@2.1.3 verbatim.
